transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Evelyn Zhou (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Opal), Liam O'Neill (Opal), Priya Rao (Opal)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to understand Opal's use-case for an in-product chat / FAQ assistant, evaluate time-to-first-token using Redwood PLG quickstart, and clarify security and deployment constraints (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samir from Redwood, happy to kick off, is this time still good?
00:15 Maya: Yeah, works great. Thanks Samir. I'm Maya, lead on the product side at Opal. We've got Liam and Priya here too.
00:30 Samir: Awesome. Quick intros? Evelyn is our solutions engineer and will handle the technical bits, especially around private deployments and the kv cache and deployment routing.
00:45 Evelyn: Hi all, excited to dig in.
01:05 Priya: Hi, thanks. High level — we're building an in-app assistant for docs + support, want low latency for chat, but cost is a factor. We also have strict data residency needs for EU customers.
01:30 Samir: Great. Can you tell us current stack — are you using hosted LLM APIs today or self-host?
01:50 Maya: Right now prototyping with OpenAI for NLU; we have an internal infra team exploring self-hosted models on prem, but that's early. The main ask is quick proof-of-value for product teams — time-to-first-token matters.
02:10 Evelyn: Ok. Our PLG quickstart is designed to get you a token in minutes. Free credits are included with the trial org; you can do a simple curl or SDK call. We can also enable streaming so UI perceives lower latency.
02:40 Liam: How fast is "minutes" — is that from signup to actual sample generation?
02:55 Samir: Yes. Typical flow: sign up, get API key, use quickstart sample repo, first token in ~5-10 minutes. If you want self-serve hosted it's quickest. Dedicated and Private require a bit of onboarding and contract discussions.
03:20 Maya: What's the difference from a performance and cost perspective between hosted and dedicated?
03:35 Evelyn: Hosted: pay-as-you-go, no infra to manage, best for quick experiments. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at volume. Private: VPC / on-prem for regulated data — more setup and licensing. Often teams start with hosted for pilot, then move to dedicated or private if they need SLOs or residency.
04:05 Priya: For EU residency we might need private. Does Redwood support KMS and customer-managed keys?
04:20 Evelyn: Yes, we integrate with KMS/HSM and can support customer-managed keys for private deployments; for hosted we offer encryption at rest, but CMK is available on private and Dedicated with certain plans. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
04:45 Maya: And SOC 2 / ISO? We need audit logs and SSO.
05:00 Samir: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation, detailed audit logs, and SAML SSO with SCIM for user provisioning. We'll attach the security pack after this call.
05:25 Liam: On the technical side, curious about latency — do you do prefix caching / kvcache?
05:40 Evelyn: Yes, the runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching. For chat workloads we keep the kv cache warm to reduce repeated compute, plus batching when throughput allows. For low-latency interactive UX we tune batch sizes to favor latency over throughput.
06:10 Maya: Right, that's helpful. How does the quickstart handle API keys and rate limits?
06:25 Samir: Trial orgs get a default quota and rate limits; you can request higher limits. We also show token-level cost breakdown in the Console so you can see per-route spend.
06:45 Priya: Can we run an initial benchmark — we want to compare Redwood hosted to our current OpenAI setup for our prompt set.
07:00 Evelyn: Absolutely, we can provision credits and run a 1k-2k prompt benchmark. For fair comparison we'll match model family and input length; we can run both latency and cost metrics.
07:25 Maya: That sounds good. What about error handling and fallbacks? For example if a region is constrained.
07:40 Evelyn: We support smart routing and fallbacks — requests can route by latency, cost or region. If capacity is constrained we can fall back to compatible model variants. This helps keep your app online.
08:05 Liam: Any limitations around structured output or function calling? We use JSON responses from the assistant.
08:20 Samir: Structured output and tool/function calling are supported in the hosted API. The SDK has helpers for streaming and structured data. Sometimes transcription shows function names weirdly but the feature works.
08:40 Maya: Great. Pricing — after free credits, what's ballpark cost for hosted?
08:55 Samir: It depends on model/throughput. For small pilots it's usage-based per token; we'll send a pricing sheet with examples. Dedicated has committed capacity discounts.
09:15 Priya: Is there a minimum for Dedicated?
09:25 Evelyn: Typically reserved capacity contracts start at monthly commitments — we'll share ranges. Many customers pilot on hosted then commit to Dedicated once they see traffic.
09:45 Maya: For our pilot success criteria: < 300ms median token latency, end-to-end 95th < 800ms, cost per 1k tokens below a threshold — we'll share numbers.
10:05 Samir: Perfect. If you share prompt set and traffic, we'll run benchmarks and quantify.
10:20 Maya: About onboarding — do you have SDKs and quickstart repos?
10:35 Samir: Yes, SDKs for Node/Python and a quickstart repo with sample prompts and UI components. We'll share a link to the quickstart and a sample curl.
10:55 Evelyn: And for enterprise security we can show how to enable SAML, SCIM and audit logging.
11:10 Liam: One question — can we bring our own models and still use Redwood's serving runtime? We have a licensed model we may want to host privately.
11:30 Evelyn: Private deployment and Dedicated can host customer models; the runtime supports bringing models, and we help with kernel selection and quantization recommendations. There is more setup for on-prem.
11:55 Priya: Good. Any gotchas when moving from hosted to private?
12:10 Evelyn: Biggest are networking (VPC peering, routing), KMS for CMK, and model format compatibility. We'll run a readiness checklist.
12:35 Maya: Ok. For the quickstart, can our PMs try self-serve or do they need an AE?
12:50 Samir: PLG quickstart is self-serve: signup, get credits, follow quickstart. AE/SE assist for benchmarks and Dedicated/Private discussions.
13:05 Priya: Great. We want the PMs to ship an experiment in two weeks.
13:15 Samir: Realistic. We'll provision trial credits today and you can start.
13:30 -- brief cross talk --
15:00 Evelyn: I'll note the EU data residency requirement — we'll highlight Private options and timeline.
15:15 Liam: Will the audit logs show token-level traces?
15:30 Samir: Yes, audit logs at the request level, but sensitive content redaction is possible. For full PII controls we recommend Private with CMK.
15:55 Maya: Any SLA on hosted?
16:10 Samir: Hosted has best-effort; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime/latency tiers. We'll share the SLA doc for Dedicated.
16:30 Priya: For the benchmarking, we care about cold-start behaviour too — how warm is the KV cache on first request?
16:50 Evelyn: Cold-start depends on model size and runtime. Cold tokens may be slower; we can run warmup sequences in the benchmark to simulate production.
17:10 Maya: Ok makes sense. We'll include cold and warm runs.
17:30 -- 20 minute silence as people take notes --
22:00 Samir: Quick recap: we'll provision a trial org, attach free credits, Evelyn will send security pack (SOC2/KMS/SSO), Opal will send prompts and traffic, then we run benchmark and reconvene.
22:25 Maya: Yep. Also can you include a checklist for dedicated and private readiness?
22:40 Evelyn: I'll attach a readiness checklist and the quickstart repo link.
22:55 Priya: One last question — do you support role-based access for routes / tokens? We want separate keys per environment.
23:15 Samir: Yes, RBAC and token-scoping per-route is supported. You can issue per-service API keys and set quotas.
23:35 Maya: Awesome. Thanks everyone.
23:45 Samir: Thanks all — we'll send the follow-ups.
23:55 End of transcript
